title: Ulyana and the Colony Revisited
premise: Vesper Eriksen, a clone of the murdered detective Ulyana Eriksen, discovers a ghost ship's manifest bearing the name of someone who died before the original's murder — proof the killing was staged to bury a secret about the colony's cryosleep capacity. Following the manifest, Vesper uncovers that the colony can only wake half its sleepers, and the original Ulyana was killed for choosing which half. In the end, Vesper must choose between exposing the truth and preserving the fragile loyalty of the crew who raised them — and chooses a third path: broadcasting the choice itself to the sleepers, letting the colony decide together.
about_author: Oscar Vane is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable internet and write about people who inherit other people's mistakes.

chapters.title: Dead Weight
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Vesper runs a routine scan on a derelict freighter and finds a manifest from a ship that never flew — listing a passenger who died years ago. The beat is quiet unease: the past tapping on the hull.

chapters.title: The Name That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Vesper investigates the impossible name, cross-referencing colonial records in a station archive. Their crewmate Dov warns them to drop it. Emotional beat: the first crack in Vesper's sense that their inherited memories are just noise.

chapters.title: Inherited Rooms
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter in Vesper's POV exploring what it means to remember Ulyana's life without living it — her apartment, her habits, her unsolved murder file. Beat: grief for someone who was never quite you.

chapters.title: Manifest Ghosts
chapters.summary: Dov's POV. Dov secretly reports Vesper's discovery to an old contact in the Colonial Trust, believing he's protecting them. Beat: loyalty curdling into betrayal, told with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Vesper boards the derelict and finds the bridge intact, logs wiped except one entry: a departure date three days after Ulyana's murder. Beat: dread sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: Half a Colony
chapters.summary: Vesper decrypts a fragment revealing the cryosleep bays can only sustain half the sleepers. Whose half was never recorded. Beat: the case stops being personal and becomes civilizational.

chapters.title: People Who Raised Me
chapters.summary: Crew POV ensemble chapter; the small crew debates whether to sell the data or pursue it. Old loyalties surface. Beat: belonging tested by opportunity.

chapters.title: The Trust Arrives
chapters.summary: A Trust enforcement vessel intercepts them, demanding the manifest. Vesper hides the decryption key inside their own neural implant — the one place clones are never searched. Beat: defiance born of being underestimated.

chapters.title: Ulyana's Last Case File
chapters.summary: Vesper finally opens the murder file fully, finding the original's notes point at the cryosleep administrator. Beat: Vesper arguing with a dead woman's handwriting, feeling less like heir and more like suspect.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: Chase sequence through debris fields as rival factions — Trust loyalists and sleeper-advocates — both hunt Vesper. Dov's POV. Beat: adrenaline laced with guilt over his report.

chapters.title: The Administrator's Daughter
chapters.summary: Vesper meets Sefa, daughter of the accused administrator, who claims her father was framed and holds the real capacity records. Beat: two children of the dead comparing inheritances.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Recovered memory chapter: Vesper's implant replays Ulyana's final hours involuntarily. She chose the half — and was killed by the person she trusted to carry out the list. Beat: horror and intimacy entangled.

chapters.title: The List
chapters.summary: Sefa and Vesper find the actual selection list hidden in the derelict's cargo bay — names chosen not by merit but by debt and favor. Beat: disillusionment; the colony's founding ideal was already rotten.

chapters.title: Turncoat
chapters.summary: Dov confesses his report to Vesper mid-crisis. A fight, then an uneasy alliance when they realize the Trust plans to seize the sleepers entirely. Beat: forgiveness as a tactical necessity that becomes something realer.

chapters.title: Wake Protocol
chapters.summary: The Trust begins unauthorized waking of 'their' half. Vesper's crew races to the cryo hub. Beat: ticking clock made literal — thaw cycles cannot be reversed.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Vesper stands before the master console holding both the list and the override. The chapter's climax of decision: refuse to choose, destroy the list, or choose better than Ulyana did. Beat: the weight of inherited authority refused.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax. Vesper transmits everything — the list, the capacity lie, the murder evidence — to every sleeper's display, then opens the choice to a colony-wide vote while stalling the Trust's forced thaws. Beat: terrifying faith in strangers.

chapters.title: The Counting
chapters.summary: Tense interlude as votes arrive in waves and Trust forces breach the hub. Dov holds the door; Sefa negotiates. Beat: solidarity forged under fire.

chapters.title: Majority
chapters.summary: The colony votes for a rotating partial awakening — no permanent half, but shared sacrifice on a schedule. The Trust, exposed, retreats. Beat: exhausted, improbable hope.

chapters.title: Case Closed, Case Opened
chapters.summary: Vesper formally closes Ulyana's murder file, naming her killer posthumously through the broadcast evidence. Beat: mourning completed at last — the clone outlives the copy's purpose.

chapters.title: First Shift
chapters.summary: The first rotation wakes; Vesper, who has never belonged anywhere, is asked to greet them as one of their own. Beat: belonging earned rather than inherited.

chapters.title: Cargo Manifest, Revised
chapters.summary: Epilogue, Vesper's POV. Back hauling cargo, but now the hold carries the first sleepers' letters home. The final line mirrors the opening scan — this time, the name on the manifest is Vesper's own. Beat: quiet, hard-won peace.
